missionPremise: The depth-warm labeller labelled CHORDS. A county ring is a digitised boundary, not a surveyed lot line, so two chords of one lot line were handed two different setbacks and a 3.44 m artifact chord could be asked to inset deeper than it is long. Measured on the dispatch's own parcel (San Marcos 48209:97658, 625-629 Sturgeon Dr, SF-6 25/5/20/15), the pre-P-262 labeller answers roles `rear side side side side_corner front side_corner side side` and is refused by three instruments at once: frontOrientation (edge 1 warm role side != fresh role rear; edges 4 and 6 side_corner != side), r32PerEdgeInset (edge 3 reads 14.98345623430401 ft and edge 7 reads 15.029472090939619 ft where the side needs 5 ft), and ground truth P2 on five chords. That is the dispatch's 'long narrow lot collapses to a false zero', reproduced before any engine code was edited.

contradicted: Four things, all recorded rather than smoothed over. (1) MY OWN CP1 ARITHMETIC for F1 was wrong: I predicted a ~1,478 sq ft envelope and applied the 25 ft front and 20 ft rear setbacks across the wrong axis; the lot is 55 ft wide and 156 ft DEEP, so the buildable envelope is 33.9 m x 13.76 m = 5,018.6 sq ft (58% of an 8,615 sq ft lot). The measurement is the correct one and the prediction was wrong. (2) MY OWN CP1 PREDICTION that the synthetic artifact ring's envelope would be IDENTICAL to its clean control's is FALSE, and is pinned as false: the labels and the verdicts ARE artifact-invariant (the scrub recovers the clean ring's own corners to 1e-12 degrees, every gate passes on both, one front line and one rear line), but the DRAWN boundary is not — the 0.05 m bump survives the offset core's mitering, giving 7 boundary vertices against 5 and 2,434.1 sq ft against 2,499.4. (3) THE DISPATCH'S DEFECT SENTENCE, carried from CP1 and still standing after implementation: 'its front is inferred from the nearest street centerline instead of the situs-named street' is FALSE on the live ring — with named roads present the R30 situs path already matched (629 STURGEON DR -> STURGEON; OSM Sturgeon Street -> STURGEON) and already picked the nearest Sturgeon edge at 7.6 m, which is also the nearest street. The reproducible pre-fix failures are the artifact-chord roles and the false zero. The dispatch's '609 Sturgeon Dr' is also wrong; the county service and the ledger-truth rail both read 629. (4) THE DISPATCH'S PREMISE 'LDT's live labeller does group ring chords into logical edges' is FALSE as stated: LDT does not group — it excludes sub-survey slivers from front candidacy and REFUSES a shape whose front is ambiguous. The deliverable is unchanged because the engine genuinely lacked the grouping, but every declared difference in the pin is generated from what LDT ACTUALLY does, not from that sentence.

leave_behind.text: P-264's per-city verification re-derive is the real grader of this lane. When it runs: 48209:97658-class rings (county rings with collinear runs and short artifact chords) should stop contributing to the residual; 324-knockout-rose-class parcels should KEEP contributing, by exactly the R32 curve-drawing reason pinned in p262-fixture-gate.test.ts. A ring that still collapses to a false zero after this lane merges is a finding, and the negative-control test is the thing to compare it against.

The curved frontage is labelled correctly and drawn incorrectly: the offset core in boundary-primitive treats a convex frontage curve as one straight segment (25 ft plus the curve's sagitta), so R32 refuses the parcel and it serves nothing. This needs a curve-aware offset (or an explicit refusal-by-name of curved frontages) in boundary-primitive, which is a different row's file. The test that pins it states which assertions flip when the core learns a curve.

The divergence test cannot see a future edit made inside LDT when no LDT checkout is present: with the checkout absent it compares against the pin, which is a recording, not a live read. The mitigation shipped (LDT commit + per-file sha256 in the pin, one-command regeneration via scripts/p262-emit-ldt-labels.mjs) is evidence, not enforcement. If R3's 'a fix in one leaves the other wrong' is to be enforced rather than measured, someone has to run the emitter in CI against a pinned LDT checkout.

Four full-suite test files cannot be parsed and two preflight-probe assertions fail on origin/main today, independent of any lane. Nobody is assigned; the suite's red baseline makes every future lane spend attention proving it is not theirs.

A labeller that resolves roles per CHORD cannot be made correct by tuning the chord rules: on a digitised ring the unit of the decision is the LOT LINE and the chords are artifacts of the digitiser. Fix the index space first (group, then label, then expand back onto the original indices), and keep the raw index space of the OUTPUT unchanged so every exact-index control and every edge-by-edge consumer keeps working. The 3.44 m chord asked to inset 4.57 m is the symptom; the index space is the disease.

Two laboratory implementations of one rule diverge in CLASSES, not in individual parcels, and the classes are uneven in value: on this fixture set 10 of 14 differences were the new behaviour (a fix owed to the other path), 1 was an A-177 deferral, and 2 were pre-existing disagreement on a curve neither path handles. A divergence test whose pin does not require a written reason per difference will average those three into 'the paths agree', which is the opposite of the truth. Make a reason-less difference FAIL and make a no-longer-differing declared difference FAIL too, so the pin cannot rot in either direction.

An artifact-vertex fixture earns its place only as a PAIR: the same lot once clean and once with duplicates and near-collinear vertices. A single artifact ring cannot separate 'the scrub worked' from 'the roles happened to come out right'. The pair also produced the lane's most useful negative result — roles and gate verdicts are artifact-invariant, but the DRAWN boundary is not (a 0.05 m bump moves the offset boundary ~0.15 m and adds two vertices), because the offset core miters on the artifact rather than ignoring it.

When a lane's deliverable depends on a second repo whose relevant directory has open PRs, take the divergence-test branch and PIN the other path's answers with its commit and per-file hashes — but write down in the close that the pin is a recording, not a check, and name the future grader. 'We verified the other path' and 'we recorded the other path' are different sentences and only one of them is true.

Do not try to bundle legacy-design-tools' labeller for a cross-repo comparison without handling module-scope imports the target function never calls: LDT's geometry.ts imports polygon-clipping at module scope, which the labeller path never executes. Aliasing it to a checked-in stub works and is honest IF the pin's method string says so; editing LDT to remove the import does not, because LDT is not this lane's to edit.

Do not try to prove a control parcel is unchanged by re-reading your own constants: run the labeller and the envelope AT THE START COMMIT and check the literals in. The 48453 control's role list and envelope coordinates are copied from the start commit's run, and that is what makes the assertion a measurement rather than a tautology about my own code.

Measured 2026-09-16 by this lane, live: 48209:97658 (Hays, 629 Sturgeon Dr, SF-6 25/5/20/15) is a 10-vertex/9-edge county ring that resolves to a 4-line lot — three collinear runs (2.14+42.11+3.44 m at 135.2 deg; 3.53+41.98+2.10 m at -44.8 deg; 11.50+5.29 m at 45.2 deg) plus a lone 16.80 m frontage line. Post-fix it labels `rear rear side side side front side side side`, verifies on every gate and passes P1-P3 with a 5,018.6 sq ft envelope; pre-fix it labels `rear side side side side_corner front side_corner side side` and is refused by three instruments at once. The lot is 55 ft x 156 ft, which is why 58% of it is buildable under 25/5/20 — and it is why my own CP1 area arithmetic (which assumed the setbacks applied across the other axis) was wrong by 3.4x.
